sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. Newguineaworld: 'Kwerba' family page, Sources section (last modified 2024-06-25).

Inventory names for the Mamberamo variety only Voorhoeve 1975: 106 (40 terms of Lake-Plain Kwerba after Bromley n.d.), Smits & Voorhoeve 1998 (Pionier-Bivak vocabulary after Buase) and Donohue 2005: 427-428 (reflexes of proto-Kwerba *s with terms from Kwerba village among others). sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa. Peta Bahasa (online edition of Bahasa dan peta bahasa di Indonesia, 2008/2018 eds.): 'Bahasa Nobuk (Kwerba)', Provinsi Papua, idb 558. Jakarta: Kemendikdasmen.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content: location, neighbouring languages (Men at Babija and Marina Valen, Manua at Eriyang, Siwaya at Sikari) and dialectometry ('isolek Nobuk (Kwerba) merupakan sebuah bahasa dengan persentase perbedaan berkisar 91%-100%' vs Armati Sarma, Dubu, Anasi, Baedate, Airo, Towe). Implies an unpublished Badan Bahasa basic-vocabulary list collected at Kampung Kwerba.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 2005. Syntactic and lexical factors conditioning the diffusion of sound change. Oceanic Linguistics 44(2): 427-442.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Only published work with first-hand lexical data from Kwerba village on the Mamberamo (pp. 427-428); Donohue normally marks stress in cited forms, so it may show or state stress placement for Kwerba Mamberamo even though its topic is *s reflexes.

sources.citation: Clouse, Duane, Mark Donohue & Felix Ma. 2002. Survey report of the north coast of Irian Jaya. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-078. Dallas: SIL International. Sec. 4.3, pp. 10-11.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Only defines 'Kwerba-Mam.' as 'the variety spoken in Kwerba, on the Mamberamo River' in the Kwerba-subfamily tree and reports consulting speakers in Kwerba (Mamberamo) village about the name Kwerba; the phoneme remarks in sec. 4.2 concern Airoran/Samarokena. Reference list: DeVries 1991 'Kwerba' (UNCEN-SIL ms) and Kim 1999 'Kwerba phonology' (unpublished ms) are both for Aurimi Kwerba [kwe].

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: Australian National University. Language index s.v. 'Nopuk' and 'Kwerba'; author entries DeVries, p. 94.
sources.note: no phonology content (bibliography). (SH)').

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU. p. 37 (entry 68 KWERBA) and p. 106 (wordlist 68a 'Lake-Plain (Br)', which Glottolog ref 126692 equates with Kwerba Mamberamo [xwr]).
sources.note: Nothing. p. 106 is a 40-item comparative wordlist after Bromley (n.d.) in plain orthography with no stress marks; p. 37 gives only names, population (+-2000) and van der Leeden's tribal names. This is the sole Glottolog reference for xwr.

sources.citation: DeVries, Jim & Sandra DeVries. 1991. Kwerba. Unpublished Research Notes on Selected Languages and Cultures of Irian Jaya 14. Jayapura/Dallas: Cenderawasih University & SIL. vi+358 pp.

sources.note: The only long description in the Kwerba family (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as a text collection/study of one feature, language code kwe); its p. 58 carries the dialect/subclassification remark Glottolog cites for Kwerba Mamberamo, so it may contain the only first-hand comparative note on the Mamberamo variety, possibly with phonology. Unpublished; a copy sits in the Glottolog/hh file store, not online.

sources.note: Records only. Glottolog's most extensive description for xwr = a wordlist or less (Voorhoeve 1975); 1 reference in total (0 descriptive). Subclassification comments cite Donohue 2005, DeVries & DeVries 1991: 58, Oosterwal 1967: 168-169. A search of all 62 Glottolog references matching 'Kwerba' shows every phonology/grammar item (Silzer 1976, de Vries & de Vries 1997, DeVries & DeVries 1991) coded to Kwerba proper [kwe].
